text.content:
When a scoundrel does something challenging, make an action roll.

  1. The player states their goal for the action.
  2. The player chooses the action rating that matches what their character is doing in the fiction.
  3. The GM sets the position for the roll.
  4. The GM sets the effect level for the action.
  5. Add bonus dice.
  6. The player rolls the dice and we judge the result.

Roll 1d for each action rating dot. +1d if a teammate assists (they take 1 stress). +1d if you push yourself (take 2 stress) or accept a Devil’s Bargain. With zero dice, roll 2d and take the lowest.

Read the single highest die. Critical (two or more 6s): you do it with increased effect. 6: full success. 4/5: partial success, with a consequence. 1-3: bad outcome.

Controlled

You act on your terms. You exploit a dominant advantage.

4/5: You hesitate. Withdraw and try a different approach, or else do it with a minor consequence: a minor complication occurs, you have reduced effect, you suffer lesser harm, you end up in a risky position. 1-3: You falter. Press on by seizing a risky opportunity, or withdraw and try a different approach.

Risky

You go head to head. You act under fire. You take a chance.

4/5: You do it, but there’s a consequence: you suffer harm, a complication occurs, you have reduced effect, you end up in a desperate position. 1-3: Things go badly. You suffer harm, a complication occurs, you end up in a desperate position, you lose this opportunity.

Desperate

You overreach your capabilities. You’re in serious trouble. Each time you roll a desperate action, mark xp in that action’s attribute.

4/5: You do it, but there’s a consequence: you suffer severe harm, a serious complication occurs, you have reduced effect. 1-3: It’s the worst outcome. You suffer severe harm, a serious complication occurs, you lose this opportunity for action.

The GM sets the consequences according to the situation. You may suffer one, some, or all of the listed consequences. You may attempt to avoid or reduce a consequence with a resistance roll.

Great: you achieve more than usual. Standard: you achieve what we’d expect. Limited: you achieve a partial or weak effect.

The GM may assess three factors that modify effect: potency (a particular weakness or advantage), quality/Tier (the effectiveness of tools, weapons or resources; fine items count +1 quality), and scale (numbers, size, scope of influence). Each factor in your favour may increase effect a level; each against you may reduce it. If effect would drop below limited, the action is impossible as stated.

You can trade position for effect, or vice versa, when it makes sense in the fiction.

1. The player chooses to resist a consequence.
  2. The GM determines if the consequence will be reduced or negated, depending on the situation.
  3. The GM determines which attribute applies (Insight, Prowess, or Resolve).
  4. The player rolls the dice for that attribute.
  5. The PC takes stress equal to 6 minus the highest die result, and the consequence is negated or reduced. On a critical, clear 1 stress instead.

Armor: mark an armor box (armor, heavy, or special) to reduce or avoid a consequence without a roll. Armor uses are recovered in downtime.

Stress: when you mark your last stress box, you suffer a trauma: clear your stress, mark a trauma condition, and you’re out of action for this scene. When you mark your fourth trauma, your character must retire.

Level 1 (lesser): less effect. Level 2 (moderate): -1d. Level 3 (severe): need help; you can’t act without assistance. Level 4: fatal or catastrophic.

If you would take harm at a level that’s full, it moves up to the next level. Push yourself to act despite severe harm.

In downtime, recover to tick your healing clock (a 4-clock). When it fills, each harm is reduced by one level.

Assist: take 1 stress to give another player +1d. You might also suffer consequences from the roll. Only one person may assist a roll.

Lead a group action: roll for each character who participates. The best single roll counts as the action result for everyone. The leader takes 1 stress for each participant who rolled 1-3.

Protect: face danger for a teammate. Step in to suffer a consequence in their place. You may roll to resist as normal.

Set up: set up another character with your action. If you achieve it, team members who follow up get +1 effect or improved position.

Fortune roll: the GM determines a dice pool (generally 1 to 4) from the trait that applies (morale, toughness, quality, Tier, magnitude…). Read the highest die: 1-3 poor, 4/5 limited, 6 full, critical exceptional.

Flashbacks: the player announces a flashback to an action performed in the past which impacts the current situation. The GM sets a stress cost: 0 for an ordinary action with easy opportunity; 1 for a complex action or unlikely opportunity; 2 or more for an elaborate action involving special opportunities or contingencies. The PC takes the stress and attempts the flashback action, rolling if it’s challenging.

Choose a plan and provide the detail. Each player chooses their load for the operation.

  • Assault: point of attack.
  • Deception: method.
  • Stealth: entry point.
  • Occult: arcane power.
  • Social: connection.
  • Transport: route.

Engagement roll: 1d for sheer luck. +1d for each major advantage, -1d for each major disadvantage (bold and daring plans, the target’s vulnerability, friends and contacts helping, crew abilities). Critical: you’ve already overcome the first obstacle and are in a controlled position. 6: controlled. 4/5: risky. 1-3: desperate.

Load: light (3) — you look like a normal citizen; normal (5) — you look like a scoundrel ready for trouble; heavy (6) — you look like an operative on a dangerous mission. Items in italics have no load.

After the score, resolve Payoff, Heat, Entanglements, then Downtime—in that order.

Payoff

The crew earns 2 rep per score, +1 per Tier the target is higher, -1 per Tier lower (minimum zero). Keep the job completely quiet and earn zero rep. Coin: 2 minor job; 4 small job; 6 standard score; 8 big score; 10+ major score. Subtract coin equal to Tier+1 if you pay a tithe.

Heat

0 smooth & quiet; 2 contained; 4 loud & chaotic; 6 wild. +1 for a high-profile or well-connected target; +1 on hostile turf; +1 if at war; +2 if killing was involved. When heat reaches 9, wanted level rises by 1 and heat resets (carrying over the excess).

Entanglements

Roll dice equal to your wanted level (0 dice: 2d, take the lowest) and read the result on the column for your heat.

Heat 0-3Heat 4/5Heat 6+
1-3Gang Trouble or The Usual SuspectsGang Trouble or QuestioningFlipped or Interrogation
4/5Rivals or Unquiet DeadReprisals or Unquiet DeadDemonic Notice or Show of Force
6CooperationShow of ForceArrest

Between scores, each PC may pursue two downtime activities, and recovers all armor uses. Additional activities cost 1 coin or 1 rep each. Add +1d if a friend or contact helps. After the roll, spend 1 coin per step to raise the result level.

  • Acquire Asset: roll the crew’s Tier. 1-3 inferior (Tier-1), 4/5 standard (Tier), 6 fine (Tier+1), critical exceptional (Tier+2).
  • Long-Term Project: roll an action and tick the project clock: 1-3 one, 4/5 two, 6 three, critical five.
  • Recover: get treatment and tick your healing clock the same way.
  • Reduce Heat: say how, roll an action and reduce heat: 1-3 one, 4/5 two, 6 three, critical five.
  • Train: mark 1 xp in an attribute or your playbook (+1 with the matching crew training upgrade). Each track may be trained once per downtime.
  • Indulge Vice: roll dice equal to your lowest attribute and clear stress equal to the highest die. Clear more than you had and you overindulge: Attract Trouble, Brag (+2 heat), Lost, or Tapped. If you don’t indulge, take stress equal to your trauma.

Status runs from -3 (war) to +3 (allies). While at war, the crew takes +1 heat from scores, temporarily loses 1 hold, and PCs get only one free downtime activity.

Development: fill the rep tracker (12, less 1 per turf held). If hold is weak, it becomes strong. If hold is strong, pay coin equal to your new Tier × 8 to advance Tier; hold becomes weak. Reset rep (keep turf).

PC xp: mark attribute xp for each desperate roll. At session end, mark 1 xp (or 2 if it happened a lot) for each trigger, on any track. Fill a track to take an advance: an action dot (attribute track) or a special ability (playbook track). Action ratings are capped at 3 until the crew unlocks Mastery.

Crew xp: at session end, mark 1 or 2 for each crew trigger. Fill the track for a new crew ability or two upgrade boxes. Each PC gets stash equal to Tier+2.
